subject: Energy
title: Solar Irradiance and Geography
description: A short lesson to help you apply Solar Irradiance and Geography.

hook.text: Solar irradiance measures how much sunlight energy hits a surface—it varies hugely by location and season.

buildup.text: The Sahara receives about 2,500 kWh/m² per year—northern Europe gets only 900–1,100 kWh/m².

discovery.text: Peak sun hours simplify comparisons—a place with 5 peak sun hours gets 5 kWh/m² of usable energy per day.

twist.text: Germany became a solar leader despite modest sunshine—proving that policy matters as much as geography.

climax.text: Solar potential is highest in deserts—but demand is in cities, creating a transmission challenge.

punchline.text: Sunshine is uneven—but solar works almost everywhere.

quiz.question: Which country became a solar leader despite modest sunshine?
